title: Giving AI Agents Memory That Learns — Jake Broekhuizen, LangChain
talk_summary: Jake argues agents should convert run traces into durable memory through a capture-analyze-update loop, filtering most evidence out and promoting only lessons. He emphasizes procedural memory updates need human review and must actually be reloaded by long-running agents.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat memory as durable context and run a read-write cycle: load relevant long-term memory into working memory, capture the run trace, filter evidence, then write only useful signal back to memory.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Memory informs the run. The run makes the evidence. We filter that evidence to make signal, and then we use that signal to update memory.

takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish procedural memory (instructions, skills, policies) as high-impact and recommend human review before committing changes into the agent's hot path.
takeaways.evidence_quote: those are probably going to drive about 75% of the behavior of my agent. And so, that actually probably should have some level of human in the loop

takeaways.technique: Keep most traces as history, not memory
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue most trace data should remain referencable history, while only a small filtered subset should become durable memory that changes future behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: most trace data actually should stay as history as referencable history

takeaways.what_they_do: They warn that long-running agents can cache runtime state so memory updates made mid-run are not available on future runs; teams must know what can and cannot be cached.
takeaways.evidence_quote: understanding what you can cache, what you can't cache to be able to make sure that memory updates are available for future runs

takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest some trace data should become offline evaluation datasets rather than memory updates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Some some might become data sets to do offline evaluations and things like that.

takeaways.what_they_do: They describe loading only relevant skills from long-term memory into working memory for the current task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: progressive disclosure with agents that actually pull in the relevant skills for a certain task
